title: Cloudflare Open Sources Decision Models for AI Agents
key_facts: During its Birthday Week, Cloudflare announced Clef, open-weight models that choose between predefined options rather than generate text.
Models: Clef (27B, multimodal) and Clef-Flash (9B); both return a probability for each allowed option in a single forward pass.
Clef takes text, JSON, images or video; Cloudflare says unlike Jev it handles images, with a 64k context window against Jev's 32k.
Cloudflare's benchmarks give Clef-Flash a median latency of 38.8 ms against 209.3 ms for Clef.
A fine-tuning service starts with Cloudflare engineer support; self-service later, no date.
Models are on Workers AI and as downloadable weights on Hugging Face.
Community commenters questioned whether this is a new category and whether benchmarks prove real reliability.
quote_evidence: During its recent "Birthday Week", Cloudflare announced Clef, a set of open-weight AI models designed to choose between predefined options rather than generate text.
Cloudflare released 9B- and 27B-parameter models, along with a platform for adapting them to specific decision-making tasks.
The company has made the Clef models available through Workers AI and as downloadable weights on Hugging Face, inviting developers to experiment with them and provide feedback.
why_it_matters_hint: Another large company has joined the race for fast, cheap 'decision models' for AI agents.
event_date: 1 Oct 2026 (Cloudflare blog date per Google News listing)
notes: InfoQ date: 8 Oct. Announcement was earlier (Cloudflare blog item dated 1 Oct 2026 in Google News results), so older news re-dated; benchmarks are Cloudflare's.
